name: HUSIC, the Hon. Edham (Ed) Nurredin

headline.note: The frozen biography supplies a near-continuous employment sequence, but not exact dates, hours, leave or substantive full-time status. Integral Energy was NSW government-controlled during Husic's tenure, while Burson-Marsteller was private; political staff, union work, party activity, study and elected office are excluded under the codebook. Missing evidence is not zero.

research_notes: The frozen official sequence is preserved even where secondary dates differ, notably the 1996–1999 CEPU role and 1999–2004 Integral Energy role.
Integral Energy is treated as government-controlled at the time; later retail sale and network rebranding do not retroactively change employer control.
The unexplained 2004–2005 transition is retained as an evidence gap rather than silently filled by candidacy or party activity.
Union and political-staff employment are excluded from the narrow headline even though they were likely paid roles.
